# Introduction

This report investigates the impact of the **1833 and 1844 Factory Acts** on the British fertility transition. Using a Difference-in-Differences (DiD) methodology, we explore whether legislative restrictions on child labor and mandatory schooling requirements acted as a catalyst for the "Quantity-Quality" trade-off.

# Data and Methodology

We utilize data from **Populations Past**, covering registration districts in England and Wales from 1851 to 1881. The primary focus is on the registration district level fertility (TFR) and textile industry intensity.

